articles.title: Fachin mantém prisão de cunhado de Vorcaro e pede manifestação da PGR sobre liberdade de ex-banqueiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente do STF também pediu manifestação do Ministério Público sobre liberdade para pai e primo de Vorcaro investigados.
articles.summary: Presidente do STF também pediu manifestação do Ministério Público sobre liberdade para pai e primo de Vorcaro investigados.
articles.body:
Daniel Vorcaro, ex-banqueiro do Master, em depoimento à PF no dia 15 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Reprodução

O presidente do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), Edson Fachin , manteve nesta quinta-feira (5) a prisão de Fabiano Zettel, cunhado do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, e pediu que a Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) se manifeste sobre os pedidos de liberdade de vários investigados no caso Master, incluindo o ex-banqueiro, seu pai Henrique Vorcaro e seu primo Felipe Vorcaro.

O presidente do STF pediu que a PGR também se manifeste sobre os pedidos de liberdade de:

Daniel Monteiro, ex-assessor jurídico de Vorcaro

Victor Lima Sedlmaier, apontado como integrante da Turma

Marilson Roseno da Silva, policial aposentado que atuaria no grupo de inteligência.

A Procuradoria também deve avaliar a manutenção de medidas cautelares contra Belline Santana, ex-chefe do Departamento de Supervisão Bancária do Banco Central, e Ana Claudia Queiroz de Paiva, sócia de uma das empresas que teria operado transferências financeiras destinadas a sustentar os pagamentos e as atividades do grupo.

Fachin manteve o uso de tornozeleira eletrônica de Leonardo Augusto Furtado Palhares, sócio de uma empresa ligada a Vorcaro.

"No caso, considerando que as medidas cautelares fixadas nos autos devem ser mantidas, porque prosseguem adequadas, necessárias e suficientes à conveniência da instrução criminal, os eventuais pedidos deautorizações deslocamentos devem ser examinadas de maneira casuística e individualizada", diz a decisão.

O presidente do Supremo também deu 3 dias para que o Complexo Penitenciário Nelson Hungria preste informações sobre o estado de saúde e assistência a Henrique Vorcaro.

Henrique Vorcaro, pai de Daniel Vorcaro — Foto: Reprodução

A unidade deve informar sobre a disponibilização dos medicamentos prescritos e às providências adotadas para a realização dos exames e tratamentos indicados pelos profissionais de saúde. Depois de receber as informações, o ministro vai ouvir a PGR.

No pedido encaminhado à Corte, a defesa anexou um relatório médico emitido em 28 de outubro de 2026. O laudo aponta episódios recorrentes de diverticulite aguda, com registro de internações hospitalares e crises.

O documento também diz que Henrique Vorcaro possui indicação para a realização de cirurgia no cólon.

Diante desse cenário, os advogados afirmam que o quadro clínico se encaixa nas hipóteses previstas em lei de conversão da prisão preventiva em domiciliar.

Fachin assumiu a análise de pedidos urgentes relacionados às investigações da Operação Compliance Zero. Desde 12 de setembro, em meio a crise institucional que se instalou no Supremo, os casos centrais do Master foram enviados à Presidência e acabaram paralisados .

Na semana passada, após parecer da PGR, o ministro fixou que anularia os pedidos apresentados pela defesas e pela Polícia Federal (PF), como prorrogação.

Nesta quinta, o presidente do STF afirmou que avaliou os casos que já tinham manifestação da Procuradoria, como o pedido de revogação da prisão de Fabiano Zettel, cunhado de Vorcaro e apontado como operador financeiro do banqueiro. Fachin manteve a prisão.

"No caso, a prisão preventiva autorizada nos autos segue adequada e indispensável à aplicação da lei penal, à manutenção da ordem pública e à conveniência da instrução criminal, devendo ser mantida", escreveu o ministro.

A PF chegou a tomar o depoimento de Zettel na tarde desta quinta-feira, por videoconferência, em desdobramento sobre as investigações do grupo chamado "a turma", apontado como um núcleo de contrainteligência, vigilância clandestina e intimidação a serviço do banqueiro e de seu pai.

Fabiano Zettel, cunhado de Daniel Vorcaro, foi preso tentando embarcar para Dubai, em um avião particular. — Foto: Redes sociais

O depoimento durou cerca de 50 minutos e Zettel disse que fazia pagamentos sem questionar. Também chegou a reclamar com investigadores que estava preso há nove meses.

articles.title: Lula diz que economia precisa estar 'arrumada' para atrair investimentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente afirmou ainda que ninguém vai querer investir em uma "economia totalmente desordenada" e que investidores levam em conta fatores como segurança jurídica e responsabilidade fiscal antes de aplicar recursos.
articles.summary: Presidente afirmou ainda que ninguém vai querer investir em uma "economia totalmente desordenada" e que investidores levam em conta fatores como segurança jurídica e responsabilidade fiscal antes de aplicar recursos.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disse nesta quinta-feira (5) que a economia do país precisa estar "arrumada" para atrair investimentos e que ninguém vai querer investir em "economia desordenada".

"Agora nós sabemos que nós temos que atrair pessoas interessadas a vim trabalhar conosco. E nós precisamos saber que para a gente atrair, a gente vai ter que ter uma economia arrumada. Ninguém vai querer vir fazer investimento numa economia totalmente desordenada. As pessoas querem saber se nós estamos falando sério".

Lula afirmou ainda que o país precisa demonstrar seriedade para atrair capital e disse que investidores levam em conta fatores como segurança jurídica e responsabilidade fiscal antes de aplicar recursos .

"As pessoas vão colocar dinheiro aqui se eles perceberem que o investimento dele vai criar o benefício para os objetivos deles e ao mesmo tempo gerar retorno financeiro para os seus investimentos. É por isso que nós temos que ter responsabilidade jurídica. É por isso que nós temos que ter responsabilidade fiscal. É por isso que a gente não pode brincar e fazer parcerias e fazer o projeto que nós estamos fazendo. Esse projeto da criação do conselho é um instante de muita seriedade desse país".

A fala ocorreu durante a 1ª reunião do Conselho para Industrialização de Minerais Críticos. O Conselho aprovou nesta quinta a lista dos minerais qualificados como críticos e estratégicos para o país . Entre eles estão terras raras, grafita, níquel, potássio e nióbio.

Na manhã desta quinta, o presidente Lula convocou o ministro da Fazenda, Dario Durigan, ex-ministros e economistas do PT para discutir medidas para a economia depois de o Banco Central interromper o ciclo de corte de juros nesta quarta (4).

Presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) durante 1ª Reunião do Conselho Nacional para Industrialização de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos — Foto: Cadu Gomes/VPR

A reunião começou por volta de 12h no Palácio da Alvorada e durou cerca de quatro horas.

Foram convidados para a reunião, além de Dario Durigan, o vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin, os ministros Bruno Moretti (Planejamento), Miriam Belchior (Casa Civil) e Esther Dweck (Gestão), os ex-ministros Fernando Haddad, Aloizio Mercadante e Guido Mantega, além dos economistas Luciano Coutinho, Eduardo Moreira e Laura Carvalho.

Após a reunião, o ministro da Fazenda afirmou que não há "fórmula mágica" para a economia brasileira e que o governo Lula vai "manter compromissos fiscais" e os feitos durante a campanha eleitoral no plano social.

articles.title: PEC da Segurança Pública: o que muda no combate ao crime no RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Aprovação da PEC da Segurança Pública pelo Senado Federal ocorreu nesta terça-feira (3).
articles.summary: A PEC da Segurança Pública aprovada no Senado prevê integração policial, atuação da PRF em hidrovias e regras rígidas para líderes de facções e milícias.
articles.body:
A aprovação da PEC da Segurança Pública pelo Senado Federal, nesta terça-feira (3), abre caminho para mudanças na organização das forças policiais e no combate ao crime organizado em todo o país. No Rio de Janeiro, onde operações policiais e confrontos fazem parte da rotina de comunidades dominadas por facções, a proposta prevê maior integração entre os governos federal, estadual e municipal, além de novas atribuições para forças de segurança.

A proposta inclui o Sistema Único de Segurança Pública (Susp) na Constituição e estabelece mecanismos para ampliar a cooperação entre as forças de segurança. O objetivo é facilitar o compartilhamento de informações e a atuação conjunta de órgãos da União, dos estados e dos municípios.

A aprovação ocorre em meio a mais um episódio de violência na capital fluminense. Nesta quinta-feira (5), uma operação policial mobilizou agentes no Complexo da Pedreira, em Costa Barros, na Zona Norte do Rio. Três ônibus e um caminhão foram usados como barricadas.

Cinco suspeitos de envolvimento com o Terceiro Comando Puro (TCP), facção que controla a região, foram presos. Entre eles, segundo as informações da operação, estava um dos chefes do tráfico.

Sistema Único de Segurança Pública passa a integrar a Constituição

Criado para organizar e integrar a atuação dos órgãos de segurança, o Sistema Único de Segurança Pública passa a ter previsão constitucional.

A proposta estabelece que a segurança pública deve ser exercida em regime de cooperação federativa, com atuação integrada e descentralizada das instituições. A intenção é ampliar a articulação entre as polícias e os demais órgãos responsáveis pela prevenção, investigação e repressão ao crime.

O texto também prevê o compartilhamento de informações e a integração dos sistemas utilizados pelas forças de segurança.

A PEC também possibilita a criação de polícias municipais, com atuação no policiamento ostensivo e comunitário.

PEC estabelece medidas mais rigorosas para líderes de facções criminosas e milícias — Foto: Reprodução

PRF poderá atuar em ferrovias e hidrovias

Outra mudança prevista é a ampliação das atribuições da Polícia Rodoviária Federal (PRF), que poderá atuar também no policiamento de ferrovias e hidrovias federais.

No Rio, a medida pode ampliar as possibilidades de atuação em rotas utilizadas para o transporte de armas e drogas, como as vias aquáticas da Baía de Guanabara. A proposta também abre caminho para uma atuação da PRF em áreas ferroviárias federais.

Regras mais rigorosas para chefes de facções e milícias

A proposta estabelece medidas mais rigorosas para integrantes de organizações criminosas, com regras específicas para quem ocupa posições de liderança em facções e milícias.

Entre as previsões estão o cumprimento de penas em unidades prisionais de segurança máxima e restrições à progressão de regime e a benefícios penais. Um dos desafios apontados no debate sobre segurança pública é impedir que chefes de organizações criminosas continuem comandando atividades ilegais de dentro dos presídios.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: Lula chama senador de pé-frio e cita processos | G1
articles.standfirst: Lula afirmou ainda que senador terá que voltar para o Brasil para responder os processos que tem na justiça. Flávio fugiu do país e desembarcou nos EUA na semana passada.
articles.summary: Lula criticou a fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro para os EUA, chamou o senador de "pé-frio" pela derrota de Donald Trump e reforçou que ele deve responder aos processos.
articles.body:
O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disse nesta quinta-feira (5) que o candidato derrotado Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) fugiu para os Estados Unidos para "pegar proteção" e o chamou de pé-frio: "chegou nos Estados Unidos e o Trump perdeu".

"Enquanto eu pegava a bandeira do Brasil, aquele gesto de pegar a bandeira nacional e levantar o povo entra numa emoção, enquanto eu fazia isso, o meu adversário pegava a bandeira americana e ficava beijando. E foi correr agora, pé frio. Derrotou o Trump, chegou nos EUA e o Trump perdeu. Foi lá para pegar proteção, você vai ver a proteção que você vai ter, você vai ter que voltar para o Brasil para receber os processos que você tem.

Flávio desembarcou em Miami na semana passada após deixar o Brasil e passar pela Argentina. O senador foi derrotado por Lula no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, realizado no dia 25 de outubro.

O senador estava proibido de sair do país após o ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal Alexandre de Moraes determinar a entrega dos passaportes de Flávio e o proibir de deixar o Brasil. Flávio descumpriu a ordem de Moraes e fugiu do Brasil.

Em uma carta divulgada após fugir do Brasil rumo aos Estados Unidos, Flávio declarou não reconhecer o resultado das urnas no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, acusou suposta fraude eleitoral e afirmou ser o "verdadeiro presidente do Brasil", o "presidente eleito".

🔎Após divulgar a primeira carta, em formato de imagens, em uma rede social, Flávio divulgou uma nova carta, também em imagens, em que substituiu as expressões "verdadeiro presidente do Brasil" e "presidente eleito" por "líder do Brasil" e "líder".

Nos Estados Unidos, o Partido Democrata conquistou na madrugada desta quarta-feira (4) a maioria das cadeiras no Senado dos EUA , impondo uma derrota histórica ao presidente Donald Trump nas eleições de meio de mandato, conhecidas como midterms.

Os democratas conseguiram "virar" sete cadeiras que estavam sob o controle republicano nos estados do Texas, Kansas, Ohio, Iowa, Maine, Carolina do Norte e Carolina do Sul. O partido de oposição também conseguiu manter outras 12 cadeiras que já ocupava no Senado.

O resultado altera drasticamente o equilíbrio de poder em Washington.

Horas depois, o partido de Donald Trump perdeu também o controle da Câmara dos Representantes. Antes da eleição, os republicanos tinham maioria nas duas Casas.

Presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) — Foto: Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

Além disso, Lula disse que a reeleição no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais "foi uma vitória para o mundo" e que na mesma semana, Benjamin Netanyahu, primeiro-ministro de Israel , e Donald Trump, presidente dos Estados Unidos, perderam a maioria nos respectivos parlamentos.

"Foi uma vitória não para o Brasil, foi uma vitória para o mundo. Mas coisa importante é que na mesma semana que eu ganhei, o Netanyahu perdeu em Israel e me parece que o meu amigo Trump está perdendo nos Estados Unidos. Então foi uma vitória, uma vitória extraordinária do povo brasileiro, foi uma lição ao mundo", disse Lula.

Lula foi reeleito presidente da República após derrotar Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno das Eleições 2026, realizado no dia 25 de outubro. O presidente teve 51,79% dos votos válidos.

A coalizão governista do primeiro-ministro de Israel, Benjamin Netanyahu, perdeu maioria no Parlamento israelens e, e obteve apenas cinco cadeiras a mais que a coalizão de oposição liderada por Gadi Eisenkot. Agora, os dois blocos travam uma corrida em busca de alianças formar novo governo, porém sem um caminho claro para chegar à maioria de 61 cadeiras.

A coalizão de Netanyahu obteve 53 cadeiras. Antes da eleição, a coalizão do premiê detinha a maioria no Knesset, com 63 assentos.

Já a coalizão de oposição, liderada por Eisenkot, obteve 48 cadeiras . Ela é formada pelos partidos Yashar, B'Yachad, Democratas e Yisrael Beiteinu.

👉 Como o Parlamento tem um total de 120 cadeiras, é necessário que uma coalizão detenha ao menos 61 assentos para formar um novo governo.

articles.title: TSE admite ação do Novo contra Lula e Alckmin por abuso de poder político   | G1
articles.standfirst: Partido apontou que o governo do presidente Lula editou 35 atos normativos, entre medidas provisórias e decretos, de 1º de janeiro a 16 de outubro de 2026.
articles.summary: Partido apontou que o governo do presidente Lula editou 35 atos normativos, entre medidas provisórias e decretos, de 1º de janeiro a 16 de outubro de 2026.
articles.body:
Lula e Alckmin em cerimônia — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/PR

O corregedor-geral do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), ministro Ricardo Villas Bôas Cueva, considerou que a ação apresentada pelo Novo contra a chapa do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e do vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), por suposto abuso de poder político nas eleições, preenche os requisitos legais para tramitar.

O ministro determinou que os citados sejam notificados para apresentar defesa no prazo de cinco dias.

Depois disso, Cueva decidirá se encerra o processo ou dá continuidade à investigação. Caso a investigação prossiga, poderão ser ouvidas testemunhas e coletadas provas para avaliar se houve abuso de poder político.

A ação do partido apontou que o governo do presidente Lula editou 35 atos normativos, entre medidas provisórias e decretos, de 1º de janeiro a 16 de outubro de 2026, criando ou ampliando benefícios.

Entre os exemplos citados está o reajuste do Bolsa Família. Para o Novo, os benefícios foram utilizados para favorecer eleitoralmente a chapa presidencial.

Ainda de acordo com a legenda, as medidas anunciadas tiveram um impacto estimado de R$ 73 bilhões. Segundo o Novo, o número equivale à soma das medidas de natureza semelhante editadas nos três anos anteriores: 17 em 2023, quatro em 2024 e 14 em 2025.

Outras 12 ações já foram apresentadas à corregedoria-geral do TSE questionando a chapa Lula-Alckmin.

Cueva também admitiu uma ação de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), candidato derrotado nas eleições, também por suposta prática de abuso do poder político, em decorrência do uso da estrutura pública de comunicação, em benefício da candidatura de Lula à reeleição.

O tribunal recebeu mais de 800 ações, mais do que o dobro das 325 no mesmo período em 2022 e das 388 de 2018.

A disputa jurídica entre as campanhas de Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) se intensificou no segundo turno, com discussões sobre estratégias nas redes sociais e distribuição de conteúdo no WhatsApp.

As ações de investigação judicial eleitoral (AIJEs) apuram suspeitas de abuso de poder político, econômico ou de autoridade e podem resultar em cassação e inelegibilidade.

Esses processos costumam ser mais demorados porque envolvem uma fase mais extensa de coleta de provas.

Segundo levantamento feito pela TV Globo e pelo g1 a partir de notas oficiais, assessorias e publicações das legendas e de seus dirigentes, 27 partidos reconheceram a vitória do petista ; o partido Novo questionou as instituições e afirmou que o país "não é uma democracia"; e uma não se manifestou.

O Novo adotou uma posição crítica e publicou uma manifestação afirmando que Lula utilizou a máquina pública para se reeleger e levantando questionamentos sobre o regime democrático brasileiro.

"Como se não bastasse fazer uma campanha cheia de mentiras, o PT usou como nunca a máquina pública e o STF para se manter no poder. Temos três ações pedindo a cassação da chapa de Lula", diz a publicação.

articles.standfirst: Preso em setembro de 2025, empresário é apontado como um dos líderes do esquema de descontos no INSS. Ele chegou a negociar uma delação premiada, mas a PGR pediu ajustes.
articles.summary: O ministro André Mendonça autorizou a prisão domiciliar do empresário Maurício Camisotti, investigado por liderar fraudes no INSS com prejuízo de R$ 6,3 bilhões.
articles.body:
O ministro André Mendonça , do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), determinou nesta quinta-feira (5) que a prisão preventiva do empresário Maurício Camisotti, investigado nas fraudes do INSS ao lado do "Careca do INSS", seja substituída por prisão domiciliar.

Camisotti é apontado como um dos líderes do esquema de descontos indevidos do INSS apurado na Operação Sem Desconto e como sócio oculto de uma entidade e beneficiário das fraudes na Previdência.

O empresário chegou a negociar um acordo de delação premiada, mas a Procuradoria-Geral da República pediu ajustes.

A decisão, que está sob sigilo, atendeu a um pedido da defesa. O ministro entendeu que há excesso de prazo na prisão e que os elementos que justificaram não permaneciam. Camisotti deve deixar a prisão na sexta-feira (6). Ele deverá cumprir prisão domiciliar em São Paulo.

A defesa do empresário afirmou que Maurício Camisotti "jamais atrapalhou o andamento das investigações".

"A liberdade deferida segue o entendimento da Suprema Casa e da legislação pátria, já que a custódia cautelar não pode, jamais, se transmutar em antecipação de pena. Aguardar-se-á o desfecho da investigação e de eventual processo e ele cumprirá todas as medidas restritivas determinadas", afirmaram os advogados Daniel Bialski e Pierpaolo Bottini.

👉 A PF afirma que associações e entidades que oferecem serviços a aposentados cadastravam pessoas sem autorização, com assinaturas falsas, para descontar mensalidades dos benefícios pagos pelo INSS.

O prejuízo, entre os anos de 2019 e 2024, pode chegar a R$ 6,3 bilhões. Em abril, quando a fraude veio à tona, o então presidente do INSS, Alessandro Stefanutto, foi demitido.

Segundo a PF e a Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), as entidades investigadas:

💰 ofereciam pagamento de propina a servidores do INSS para obter dados de beneficiários;

✍️ usavam assinaturas falsas para autorizar descontos;

💻 criavam associações de fachada , muitas vezes presididas por idosos, pessoas de baixa renda ou aposentados por incapacidade.

As associações cadastravam, sem autorização, aposentados e pensionistas do INSS e passavam a descontar mensalidades diretamente na folha de pagamento. Em muitos casos, os idosos nem sabiam que estavam sendo "associados".

Há registros de aposentados que, no mesmo dia, foram filiados a mais de uma entidade — com erros de grafia idênticos nas fichas, apontando para fraudes.

De acordo com a PF, dirigentes e servidores do INSS recebiam vantagens indevidas para facilitar a inserção dos descontos nos contracheques dos aposentados, enquanto associações de fachada viabilizavam o desvio.

A investigação começou em 2023 na CGU, no âmbito administrativo. Em 2024, após a CGU encontrar indícios de crimes, a Polícia Federal foi acionada.

articles.title: El-Sayed calls Vance habibi in victory speech. What does it mean?
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed referred to Vice President JD Vance as "habibi" in election night remarks. Here's what the Arabic term means.
articles.body:
In a nod to his Arab heritage, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed jokingly used an Arabic term of endearment in reference to Vice President JD Vance while speaking to supporters on election night.

In an election night speech, El-Sayed celebrated the "delicious irony" of Vice President JD Vance being the person who will swear in the newly elected senator when the next Congress takes office in January 2027, calling Vance "habibi," an Arabic word meaning my love or my sweetheart.

El-Sayed, who is Arab American, used the Arabic term while making remarks to Democratic supporters in Detroit ahead of his election win for Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat.

The former Wayne County and Detroit health director of Egyptian descent will become the first Muslim U.S. senator after defeating Republican and former U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers in the Nov. 3 election.

Here's what to know about El-Sayed's use of the Arabic term.

articles.title: Former Trump staffer calls for Wiles to resign over midterm wipeout
articles.summary: Caroline Sunshine, a former staffer to President Trump, on Wednesday called for White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to resign over the massive losses Repu...
articles.body:
Caroline Sunshine, a former staffer to President Trump, on Wednesday called for White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to resign over the massive losses Republicans saw in the midterm elections.

Sunshine told Fox News's Jesse Watters on "Jesse Watters Primetime" that she was going to say "what a lot of people are saying privately."

"Susie Wiles needs to resign," she told Watters, causing the host to raise his eyebrows. "She needs to offer her resignation to the president before he has to ask for it. Her campaign skills have not translated into governing. Susie was behind the historic win in 2024, and she deserved credit for it and got the top job for it."

The former Trump staffer added that Wiles was now "behind the historic loss where we lost Mississippi and have lost potentially the Senate for six years, and so that cuts both ways."

The Mississippi Senate race remains tight between Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.) and Democrat Scott Colom and has not been called by The Hill's election partner Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ). Colom leads Hyde-Smith with 49.04 percent of the vote to her 48.85 percent, according to DDHQ.

Sunshine said Wiles remaining in her role could cost Republicans again in 2028 and that "if she loves and respects the president and his legacy, she'll do the right thing and step aside."

"And a lot of this was staff failure, a lot of this was strategy and messaging failure," Sunshine said. "It's the chief of staff's job to manage the staff. ... Why wasn't the staff out messaging?"

Reporting before the midterms suggested Wiles could leave the White House after the midterms. Politico reported last month that Trump had received negative feedback about Wiles from allies, though he called the story " TOTAL FAKE NEWS " and said Wiles "has my COMPLETE confidence."

Trump has also publicly praised Wiles on numerous occasions. After Wiles announced she had been diagnosed with breast cancer earlier this year, Trump referred to her as "an amazing person" and "an amazing fighter." Wiles announced in September that she was cancer free .

Former White House chief of staff Mick Mulvaney told NewsNation's "The Hill Sunday" that he expects her to leave her post after the midterms, though not because "she's fallen out of favor with Trump."

"It's just a natural sort of time to make that change," he added.

Sarah Matthews, a former White House deputy press secretary in Trump's first term, told MeidasTouch in October that the president was not pleased "with the way things are right now" and had floated replacement ideas to allies. She suggested that he floated the idea of replacing Wiles with the deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, an idea Matthews described as "a terrifying prospect ."

articles.title: Carville declares DeSantis ‘Republican winner’ after midterms
articles.summary: Democratic strategist James Carville suggested Wednesday that Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) was the 2026 midterms’ “Republican winner” after Democrats made s...
articles.body:
Democratic strategist James Carville suggested Wednesday that Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis (R) was the 2026 midterms' "Republican winner" after Democrats made sweeping gains across the country and reclaimed both chambers of Congress.

Carville, political adviser Mark McKinnon and Gen Z for Change founder Aidan Kohn-Murphy were talking about the potential for a post-President Trump GOP on Carville's " Politics War Room " podcast when he made his claim about the Florida leader.

"The Republican winner last night was Ron DeSantis," he said. "But Ron DeSantis can say we did better in — you know, 'We want to win? Look at what we did in Florida' ... If I'm not a Republican, I don't like Ron DeSantis ... But everybody had dismissed him as out of hand."

Carville noted that the Republican Party's image will go down following Tuesday's losses, but DeSantis's "stock ... doubled in the last 24 hours." McKinnon chimed in, saying Florida's and Texas's results starkly differed, with Democrats making major gains in the Lone Star State while Republicans held firm in Florida, crediting DeSantis.

"The greatest beneficiary of this election may be Ron DeSantis," he added.

Kohn-Murphy added that Democratic gains, but not wins, in Florida were "a pretty devastating result" that "could have been better." But after seeing the Republican governor on the "national stage" before, the activist said he was unsure if "people will really take him seriously."

DeSantis, who entered office in 2019 with Trump's support and praise until the two faced off during the 2024 Republican presidential primary, has been seen as a potential successor to the president's legacy. The Never Back Down PAC presented the governor as the future of the GOP in 2023.

Democrats gained ground in Florida state races and defeated Republican candidates for House seats, although the GOP maintained control of other major statewide offices. Voters chose Rep. Byron Donalds (R-Fla.) to succeed the term-limited DeSantis, becoming the Sunshine State's first Black governor.

The outgoing Florida governor called the outcome of the midterms an " extinction-level event " for Republicans across the country while the party narrowly hung on to Florida.

"In January, when everyone in office leaves who are either term-limited or got voted out, of the 10 largest states in this union, only one state will have Republican control … the state of Florida," he said at a press conference Wednesday.

DeSantis also diagnosed the election result as "no question ... a rebuke of the president and the Congress by Democrats, independents and some Republicans that crossed over," in an interview with Fox News's Laura Ingraham later Wednesday.

"But a lot of our voters who stayed home, they stayed home because they were frustrated with the lack of productivity from Republicans in the House and Senate," he continued. "That's just a fact. They were promised big things, and they didn't deliver it."

articles.title: House conservative emerges with 2028 presidential pick after GOP's midterm massacre: 'I am all in'
articles.summary: A House Freedom Caucus original member says he's backing Marco Rubio for 2028, urging the GOP to shift immigration messaging after midterm losses.
articles.body:
One of the original members of the House Freedom Caucus has made his decision on who to support in 2028 after Republicans' historic losses in Tuesday night's midterms.

Rep. Marlin Stutzman, R-Ind., told Fox News Digital "I am all in" for Secretary of State Marco Rubio and called on fellow Republicans to begin thinking about how to rebuild in the wake of their election losses.

He also told Fox News Digital that Republicans "have to do better at communicating" since they "can't push policy" after losing the House and Senate majorities.

Among those communication changes, he suggested changing the way Republicans discuss immigration.

"We need to get off the deportation messages, take credit for closing the border, and now start finding a path forward for those here illegally obeying the laws," Stutzman said. "No citizenship just work visas."

A blue tsunami swept both federal and state races on Tuesday night. In the House, both battleground districts and seats considered safe GOP strongholds saw upset Democrat victories.

Dozens of races have yet to be called, but Democrats are projected to hold at least 54 seats in the Senate . In the House so far, they're projected to win 240 seats, compared to 147 projected for Republicans.

Democrats also scored upset victories in multiple governorships, namely in Texas and Iowa.

And within hours of the writing landing on the wall, various GOP factions began publicly discussing how to rebuild and move forward.

Vice President JD Vance quickly distanced himself from the war in Iran, which is thought to be one of the biggest drivers of voters moving away from the GOP.

"The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance posted on X in a lengthy statement. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

Vance is considered a top presidential contender for Republicans in 2028, as is Rubio.

But it's not clear yet whether their senior roles in the Trump administration will similarly sandbag their prospective bids.

articles.title: DOJ civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns, says White House asked her to wait until after midterms
articles.summary: Harmeet Dhillon resigned Thursday as the Department of Justice's assistant attorney general for civil rights, sources told Fox News.
articles.body:
Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon is resigning as head of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, telling Fox News Digital exclusively that she made the decision weeks before Republicans' midterm losses and was asked by White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to delay her departure until after the election.

"I wasn't asked to resign," Dhillon told Fox News Digital. "I resigned three weeks ago, and Susie asked me to please wait until after the midterms."

Dhillon formally submitted her resignation on November 5, according to a letter obtained by Fox News Digital.

Dhillon said she informed Wiles three weeks before Election Day that she believed she had "accomplished everything" she came to Washington to do and wanted to return to private practice.

Asked if she would testify before Congress if subpoenaed after leaving the administration, Dhillon said there would be limits on what she could discuss because of executive privilege but indicated she would seek legal advice and follow it.

"I would certainly take legal counsel and follow it in that regard," she said.

Dhillon was also asked whether she expected Trump to pardon her or other administration officials if congressional Democrats sought to target them.

"I have no idea. I haven't ever discussed that with him, asked for it," Dhillon said. "And I have done nothing, in my opinion, that would require that, but, you know, that's up to the president."

She revealed that the decision to leave the DOJ ultimately came down to wanting to return to the work she had done for much of her career in the private sector.

Dhillon moved to Washington following the deaths of her husband and father to "serve my country," but after roughly two years in the administration, she believed the time has come to leave.

"My decision, my choice," Dhillon said. "It's time."

"Today, I accepted the resignation of Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon," Attorney General Todd Blanche wrote on X. "She has defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor. The Department is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors."

She was nominated by President Donald Trump in December 2024 and was sworn into office in April 2025 after being confirmed by the Senate. She is leaving after Trump's Republican Party lost the House and Senate in this week's midterm elections.

In the lead-up to the midterms, Dhillon defended the Trump administration's investigation into noncitizen voters.

"There are people who feel that the point is to sow distrust about the whole election system. There are very few people who are noncitizens who end up voting — very, very few. And so, therefore, what's the purpose?" Lesley Stahl, host of CBS' "60 Minutes," had asked Dhillon.

Dhillon's departure caps a roughly 19-month tenure in which the longtime conservative attorney carried out a sweeping overhaul of the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, shifting its priorities toward issues including DEI and race-conscious policies, religious discrimination, transgender participation in women's sports, Second Amendment rights and election integrity.

The transformation also brought extraordinary turnover inside the division, with roughly 300 attorneys departing during Trump's second term, according to recent reports. Dhillon has aggressively sought to rebuild its ranks, telling Fox News Digital that she recruited more than 130 lawyers during her tenure.

Before joining the administration, Dhillon founded the Dhillon Law Group and the Center for American Liberty and built a national profile litigating First Amendment, election law and other civil-rights cases. A longtime Republican Party official and Trump ally, she was nominated by Trump in December 2024 and confirmed by the Senate in April 2025.

Her appointment drew fierce opposition from Democrats and some traditional civil-rights groups, while conservatives argued that she would redirect a division they believed had become ideologically tilted under previous administrations.

"We changed it, and that's what we came here to do. And it's done," Dhillon told Fox News Digital.

Fox News Digital's Lindsay Kornick and Hanna Panreck contributed to this post.

articles.title: Ohio's most popular midterm Republican says election results hold a warning for Dems
articles.summary: Frank LaRose says the Republican Party must refocus on human freedom and free market principles after GOP candidates struggled on Election Day.
articles.body:
Ohio's most popular midterm Republican says his party needs to refocus its message into a constructive appeal to voters if the GOP hopes to regain the ground it lost on Election Day.

Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose won his race to become Ohio State Auditor on Tuesday night, securing over 2.3 million votes, a total that easily eclipsed any other statewide Republican candidate.

Gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy secured just over 2 million votes in his race, and Sen. Jon Husted secured just under 2.1 million votes in his bid for re-election.

"There are, of course, cycles to American politics, but also I think we as a party need to focus on what we're for, not just what we're against," LaRose told Fox News Digital in an interview. "I mean, we know what we're against. The other side has a bunch of crazy ideas that are dangerous for the future of our states and our nation, but we need to get back to talking about what we're for. We're the party that stands for human freedom, that idea that we're endowed by our Creator with rights, those don't come from government."

"Protecting human freedom, protecting free market principles that people can prosper by, you know, the sweat of their own brow and working hard to build a business, those are really kind of the bread and butter conservative issues that drove me to become a Republican when I first started thinking about politics as a young man myself," he continued.

LaRose went on to point to Ohio Issue 3, a ballot measure requiring Ohio voters to present voter ID when casting their ballots. The overwhelmingly Republican-backed measure sailed through Tuesday's election with over 65% of the vote, even as Republican candidates struggled.

LaRose argued that the measure presents a warning to the midterm election's victorious Democrats that Republican policies remain popular even if candidates fail in their messaging.

"Candidly, I wish more conservatives had showed up to vote yesterday, and I think the outcome might have come out a little different. But even among most people that consider themselves Democrats in Ohio, it doesn't compare to Democrats on the coast, right? The East Coast and the West Coast is more of that kind of, you know, woke DEI cuckoo wing of the party. But even in Ohio, most Democrats are pretty common sense people, and of course, showing your ID to vote is common sense," LaRose said.

"Let this be a message to my friends from the other side of the aisle that won their elections in Ohio. Remember that Ohio is not a far left state when it comes to common sense kind of things," he added. "Govern like a Midwestern Democrat and maybe you'll be all right, but if you govern like a coastal Democrat, then I think your time in office is going to be short."

As Ohio's secretary of state , LaRose had a front-row seat as election tallies started mounting. He said it became clear with around 60% of the vote tallied that Republicans were not going to have a good night.

Nevertheless, he thanked Ohio's 40,000 election workers for their professionalism throughout the election process. LaRose has served as Ohio's elections chief for eight years, and he says his move to state auditor will allow him to keep Ohio's politicians accountable for their spending.

"When they waste your money, we're going to make them infamous, and when they steal your money, we're going to lock them up," he said.

articles.title: DAVID ASMAN: Democrats exploit gas-price pain while ignoring their own record
articles.summary: From the Keystone XL pipeline cancellation to carbon tax proposals, Democrats have a long history of policies that have driven gas prices higher.
articles.body: The incredible irony of this election is that Democrats won largely on the issue of higher gas prices…when those same Democrats have done everything they can to raise gas prices when they’ve been in power. The very first executive order that President Biden signed on his first day in office was cancelling the 1,200-mile-long Keystone XL pipeline, which would have brought 830,000 barrels of Canadian oil a day into U.S. refineries. The U.S. Gulf Coast refineries that the Keystone pipeline would have served are built and optimized to process Canada’s heavy, sour crude oils — like Alberta tar sands/bitumen — into high volumes of diesel and jet fuel. That is exactly the kind of fuel we’re in most need of right now. And it wasn’t just President Biden. On February 24, 2015, President Barack Obama vetoed the Keystone XL Pipeline Approval Act passed by Congress. An attempt in the Senate to override Obama’s veto failed on March 4, 2015. DUFFY UNLEASHES ON BUTTIGIEG WITH SWIPE OVER WHICH ADMIN HAS ACCOMPLISHED MORE: 'MOVED LIKE A SLOTH' Other Democrat presidential contenders are on record favoring a carbon tax, which would have an immediate effect on raising gas prices. On Sept 4, 2019, Kamala Harris said, "Under my plan there will be a carbon fee." Likewise, Pete Buttigieg campaigned on the idea of an expensive carbon tax, saying, "I propose that we assess a carbon tax. I know you’re not supposed to use the "T" word when you’re in politics, but you might as well call this what it is." When Buttigieg became secretary of Transportation under President Biden, he worked hard trying to get auto companies to switch from gas-powered cars to EVs, even though consumers weren’t buying and car companies and dealers were left warehousing thousands of unsold vehicles. GM absorbed $11.2 billion in losses and cancellation of its EV infrastructure plans. Ford eliminated entire models, such as its electric F-150 truck, which Buttigieg promoted and President Biden test drove in Dearborn, Michigan, in May 2021. Eventually, Ford took a $19.5 billion EV write-down. But through it all, Buttigieg insisted that EV buyers would never go back to gas-powered cars…even after a brutal winter when EV owners in Chicago and elsewhere swore they’d never buy another EV, as batteries failed to function in the cold weather. Of course, the younger generation of Democrat presidential contenders is just as eager to raise your gas prices. Rep Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s "Green New Deal" was shoehorned, in part, into President Biden’s infamously named "Inflation Reduction Act." The Act's multi-trillion-dollar green energy spending boondoggle became a major factor in the Biden administration’s 21.5% cumulative inflation, which is still part of the unaffordability crisis that Democrats blame on President Trump. All these lame-brain ideas and unworkable investments ended up creating big increases at the pump that dwarf today’s prices. The gas prices under President Obama peaked at $4.55 a gallon, in some areas, in May 2011. Inflation adjusted, that would be $6.78 today. Gas peaked under President Biden at $5.03 in June 2022. That would be $5.79 today. And the highest spike hike under President Trump was $4.55 a gallon in mid-May of this year. JEFFRIES CALLS OUT TRUMP-ERA GAS PRICES AFTER TELLING REPUBLICANS NOT TO POLITICIZE PUMP PAIN UNDER BIDEN President Trump claims that once the Iranian war is over, gas prices will come back to the $3 level we saw just before the war began. But voters became understandably frustrated with the president’s failed estimates of when the war will end. We did see oil prices drop dramatically when it looked like we had an Iranian deal in April. But exactly when the war is over, we don’t know. articles.title: Opinion - Nikki Haley is wrong! Democrats won midterms, Republicans didn’t just lose
articles.summary: Republicans can learn from their losses. But they should be careful not to explain away Democratic victories as if the candidates themselves had nothing to d...
articles.body:
Republicans are so busy explaining why voters rejected them that they aren't acknowledging why voters intentionally chose several Democrats. Check out Nikki Haley on the "TODAY Show": "I think for me what it was is I don't think Democrats won, I think Republicans lost for themselves."

Yes, Republicans have serious problems. Yes, President Trump's approval ratings, the economy, the war and the cost of living played a role. But to reduce what happened Tuesday to a Republican rejection of Trump is to dismiss the candidates Democrats put forward and the campaigns they actually ran.

Look at Texas. Gina Hinojosa didn't just ride an anti-Trump wave into the governor's mansion. She became the first Latina governor in Texas history, defeating Republican incumbent Greg Abbott and ending decades of Republican control of the governor's office.

A civil rights and labor attorney who spent years in the Texas Legislature, Hinojosa built a campaign around affordability, public education, corporate influence and the everyday concerns of working families. She connected with Latino voters by speaking directly to her roots in the Rio Grande Valley and the experiences of communities that often feel overlooked. And her argument was bigger than Trump — it spanned 20 years! Republicans have controlled Texas government for decades. She challenged voters to consider what that prolonged control had actually delivered, and they said, not enough.

Then there's James Talarico, who won Texas's U.S. Senate race. He resisted the temptation to get dragged into every culture-war confrontation, although everyone tried to reel him in, and instead focused on economic populism: health care costs, corporate power and the divide between the wealthy and working people. As a Type 1 diabetic, he spoke personally about the cost of insulin. He also deliberately appealed to voters of faith. He has extreme message discipline. He also understood that winning voters mattered more than winning arguments on social media.

Now, let's go to Georgia. Keisha Lance Bottoms made history as the first Black woman elected governor in American history. But her campaign wasn't built on symbolism alone. The former Atlanta mayor emphasized Medicaid expansion, affordable housing, higher wages, education and the cost of living. She won despite Republican businessman Rick Jackson pouring more than $200 million of his own money into the race. And there was more than a decade of intentional infrastructure that helped make Georgia competitive. Stacey Abrams spent years building political power, challenging voter suppression and expanding Democratic participation through organizations like Fair Fight Action. Bottoms's victory didn't happen in magically because Republicans failed — it came after years of organizing, coalition-building and political groundwork by Black women across the state.

Look at South Carolina, too. Annie Andrews flipped a Senate seat Republicans had held since 1998. She's a pediatrician who campaigned on health care access, affordability and fighting corruption. She got criticism from her own party for being too moderate. She understood her audience and positioned herself as a pragmatic alternative. Yes, questions about nepotism and Trump's involvement in Darline Graham's rise created vulnerabilities. But Andrews still had to persuade voters to choose her

And in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers, understanding that health care costs have skyrocketed since Trump took office and premiums are increasing by an average of 13 percent nationwide next year. He ran on universal health care being a flagship policy, working-class economics and taking corporate money out of politics.

Democrats deserve a lot of credit for these victories. These candidates built coalitions, specifically understood their states, made strategic decisions and offered voters something to vote for.

Republicans can learn from their losses. But they should be careful not to explain away Democratic victories as if the candidates themselves had nothing to do with it.

Lindsey Granger is a NewsNation contributor and co-host of The Hill's commentary show "Rising." This column is an edited transcription of her on-air commentary.

articles.title: Abandoning pro-life voters helped cause GOP midterm losses, pro-life org says
articles.summary: (The Center Square) – A pro-life organization says that Republicans got the results they earned in the 2026 midterm elections, arguing that ignoring its base...
articles.body:
(The Center Square) – A pro-life organization says that Republicans got the results they earned in the 2026 midterm elections, arguing that ignoring its base of pro-life voters leading up to the election by relative inaction in the abortion drug review and shying away from confronting mail-order abortion policies is clearly not a winning tactic for the GOP.

President of Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America Marjorie Dannenfelser told The Center Square: "Rule number one of politics is: don't abandon your base."

"This election wasn't a blue wave, it was a blue tsunami, because the GOP ignored its base," Dannenfelser said.

Election analysts and polls have shown that continued his inflation and cost-of-living concerns, and the ongoing conflict in Iran that has led to higher gas prices despite President Donald Trump's vow during the 2024 campaign that he would not get the U.S. into more "forever" wars, are the main reasons Republicans lost so badly.

Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America (SBA) has detailed previously what they consider the importance of the pro-life vote to Republican candidates. According to SBA , Trump won 91% of the pro-life vote in the 2024 presidential election, but would have lost if one to two percent of these voters had not turned out.

Marjorie Dannenfelser said that as SBA's voter contact program ahead of the midterms "reached nearly 4 million voters at their doorsteps, our canvassers found almost zero pre-existing enthusiasm among pro-life voters for Republican candidates this election.

"And it's no wonder why," Dannenfelser said. "Not only were Republicans silent on the abortion issue, but abortions have gone up since the Dobbs decision [that returned abortion decisions to the states] and the administration has left Joe Biden's mail-order abortion drug policy in place.

"Their calculation that delaying action on abortion drugs would help Republicans in the midterms was a complete miss," Dannenfelser said.

SBA ran a voter contact program ahead of the 2026 midterms, where canvassers went door to door explaining to pro-life voters and persuadable pro-life voters the "pro-life message" as well as "Democrats' extremism on issues like late-term abortion and infanticide."

SBA invested $80 million into the 2026 midterm elections in the efforts to ensure a pro-life majority in the House and Senate, The Center Square reported .

SBA put a vast amount of effort in the 2024 election as well with the "largest pro-life voter contact in history" that reached more than 10 million voters and made over 4 million house visits to battleground states, helping to win the presidency, flip the Senate, and hold the House, as stated by SBA .

Dannenfelser told The Center Square that "Republicans have a hard lesson to learn ahead of 2028.

"The GOP must stop running from the pro-life fight and start giving voters a reason to fight for them," Dannenfelser said.

"Allowing the mail-order abortion drug status quo and parroting the pro-choice position of 'leaving abortion to the states' are not winning strategies, either to save lives or to win votes," Dannenfelser said.

"We're going to spend the next few years working to make that happen, and we hope leaders in the party will do the same," Dannenfelser said.

Dannenfelser warned that "pro-abortion Democrats are going to do extreme things with majorities in Congress."

"In their first 100 hours, they have promised to pass the so-called Women's Health Protection Act which would ban states from having pro-life laws and establish abortion until birth nationwide," Dannenfelser said.

Additionally, these Democrats have "committed to eliminating the Hyde Amendment so that taxpayers are forced to fund these abortions," Dannenfelser said.

"Republicans must stand strong against this, expose it, and more boldly step into the fight for life," Dannenfelser said. "There's still time for them to get this right ahead of 2028."

Although Virginia voted to allow abortion up to birth this past Tuesday, Idaho voters rejected the ballot initiative that would allow for late-term abortions.

SBA released a memo directly following the 2026 midterms, where Dannenfelser stated that "Republican consultants got the campaign they wanted — and the defeat they earned."

articles.title: Head of DOJ Civil Rights Division resigns after GOP midterms loss
articles.summary: Harmeet Dhillon oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, targeting universities and focusing on culture war issues.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — Harmeet Dhillon, the Republican attorney who oversaw a massive overhaul of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, submitted her resignation Thursday. Attorney General Todd Blanche posted on X that he has accepted Dhillon’s resignation. He wrote that she “defended the civil liberties of every American and enforced the law without fear or favor” and that the DOJ “is grateful for her dedicated public service, and we wish her every success in her future endeavors.” Dhillon posted Thursday on X that the job had been the “honor of a lifetime.” “We ushered in the downfall of illegal DEI, we fought to protect women and girls’ sports, and so much more,” she wrote. The departure of Dhillon, who had a long history of working as an election lawyer for the GOP, comes just two days after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the midterm elections. Under Dhillon’s leadership, the Civil Rights Division led some of the Trump administration’s most controversial legal maneuvers, including lawsuits that cited claims of discrimination at elite universities. The division declined to open a use-of-force investigation into the ICE officer who shot and killed Renee Nicole Good in Minnesota earlier this year. Her office also filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., in an effort to obtain voter registration lists from the states in the months before the election, with federal judges dismissing 27 of those cases. Dhillon was a regular presence on conservative media in the run-up to Tuesday’s elections, promoting the work of the Civil Rights Division. Dhillon is set to speak at the Donald Trump Ballroom at the Mar-a-Lago Club during the Conservative Political Action Committee’s Circle Retreat and Gala on Thursday. Bloomberg Law first reported her resignation plans. Dhillon’s office recently attempted to indict Cassidy Hutchinson, the former Trump administration official who testified before the House Jan. 6 committee about Trump’s actions during the Capitol siege. Her office also brought a criminal case against former CNN journalist Don Lemon and protesters over a demonstration at a church in Minnesota under a statute historically used to protect reproductive rights facilities. Stacey Young, the executive director of the group Justice Connection, called Dhillon “the most destructive, lawless, and hateful head of the Civil Rights Division in DOJ history,” and said in a statement that she “wielded the enormous power of the Justice Department to threaten universities, state and local officials, and election workers in spurious cases that rarely won in court.” Dhillon “decimated” the Civil Rights Division, Young said, and called on the incoming Senate “to exercise its full advice and consent powers to ensure the next Assistant Attorney General fulfills the division’s congressional mandate to enforce all Americans’ civil rights diligently and fairly.” Kristen Clarke, the NAACP’s general counsel and the former chief of the Civil Rights Division during the Biden administration, said Dhillon “abdicated her responsibility to enforce our nation’s federal civil rights laws and destroyed the crown jewel of the Justice Department.” Clarke said in a statement that Dhillon “abandoned cases, purged the work force and weaponized the Division to target institutions to achieve illegitimate, partisan goals” and that the NAACP would demand that her replacement “respect the agency’s sacred mission, enforce the law fairly, and protect our civil rights.”

images.caption: Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights Harmeet Dhillon, left, and first Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli announced the findings of a federal investigation into alleged sexual abuse of female inmates by staff on Aug. 13, 2026, in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Schumer faces mutiny from newly elected Senate Dems as party prepares to seize power
articles.summary: Senate Democrats face a leadership battle as Chuck Schumer seeks to keep his role, but several newly elected senators are pushing for new blood.
articles.body: Senate Democrats will soon decide who will lead them with their newly acquired grip on power in the upper chamber, and while Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., appears to be the favorite, some in the caucus aren’t eager to back him. Schumer has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade, helming the caucus as both majority and minority leader since 2017. But many of the fresh crop of Democratic senators-elect, which spans the ideological gamut from moderate to progressive, are tepid, at best, in backing him for another term. And some said throughout their campaigns that they wouldn’t support him at all. DEM SENATE HOPEFUL REJECTS SCHUMER BUT BENEFITS FROM MILLIONS IN SPENDING BY HIS ALLIES "I mean no disrespect for Chuck Schumer, but we need new leadership," Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton told CNN in September. "We need new younger leadership, young blood." Hamilton is the moderate megachurch pastor who toppled Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., on Election Night, flipping the Sunflower State for the first time in nearly a century. He, like others this cycle, argued that Democrats needed "fresh ideas and fresh leadership." "In Kansas, Chuck Schumer is a liability for Democrats, and we've got to have leaders that can unite us, bring us together, not just Democrats, but bring together Democrats and Republicans to solve real problems," he said. "And I think people are frustrated with the gridlock in the sense that people are not working together to solve problems." Democrats are expected to hold their leadership elections later this year, and Schumer will have to shore up support within his newly expanded caucus to stay at the top. But he will only need a majority of Senate Democrats to back him. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: CONGRESS BRACES FOR POST-ELECTION GAME OF MUSICAL CHAIRS AS LEADERSHIP BATTLES LOOM So far, Democrats’ majority in the upper chamber is at 54 seats and could further expand depending on the results in Mississippi and Alaska, which as of Thursday were leaning in their favor. Schumer believed that he would still be the one to lead Democrats and contended to reporters on Wednesday that issues that incoming senators and their voters may have had with the direction of the Democratic Party in recent years were not about him. "The issue is not me," Schumer said. "I'll be re-elected as majority leader, but the issue is focusing on the American people and what they want." Still, there is a faction of newcomers, including senators-elect Troy Jackson in Maine, Julianna Stratton in Illinois, Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, who aren’t all in for Schumer. THUNE GOES ALL-IN ON CAMPAIGN TRAIL AS SCHUMER STAYS ON BENCH, FACES REJECTION FROM FELLOW DEMS Jackson, speaking to reporters just before Election Day, said his position hadn’t changed on Schumer. "I told Schumer that I’m going to, you know, support somebody else," Jackson said. "So it’s no different now." That somebody else could be Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., who has been proposed as an alternative by progressives, like El-Sayed, to lead Senate Democrats instead of Schumer. Van Hollen may have his eyes elsewhere — he has said that he’s "kicking the tires" on a 2028 run. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP A Democratic aide familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking told Fox News Digital that before selecting a new leader, the lawmaker believed "the caucus needs to have an honest and open conversation about how we move an agenda forward that reflects the will of the American people." "He’s made it clear that the new Democratic majorities need to use their power to push a proactive, economic agenda," they said.

articles.title: Pedro Sánchez se desmarca de los nuevos detenidos en el 'caso Koldo': "Ninguna de esas personas tiene nada que ver conmigo"

articles.summary: El presidente del Gobierno ha negado cualquier vínculo
articles.body: El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha negado cualquier vinculación con los seis detenidos este jueves por la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil en una nueva pieza secreta del 'caso Koldo'. Durante una rueda de prensa en Madrid tras la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana, el líder del Ejecutivo ha zanjado la cuestión afirmando de forma tajante: "Ninguna de esas personas tiene nada que ver conmigo". Tras ello, el jefe del Ejecutivo ha minimizado el impacto de la operación policial asegurando que "no es nada nuevo" y que es una causa bajo investigación judicial desde hace varios años. Además, ha reiterado su "total colaboración con la justicia". El líder del PSOE también ha aprovechado la comparecencia para exigir explicaciones a Alberto Núñez Feijóo por las acusaciones de que un abogado vinculado al PP habría ofrecido dinero a Koldo García a cambio de declarar en contra del entorno socialista: “Creo que ante estas acusaciones tan graves que se están vertiendo sobre el Partido Popular, el señor Feijóo tendría que dar alguna explicación. He tratado de ser lo más breve posible”. El secretario general del Partido Popular (PP), Miguel Tellado, ha arremetido contra el presidente del Gobierno, señalando que entre los detenidos se encuentra Cristian Corvillo, supuestamente vinculado como su exchófer en las primarias del PSOE del año 2017. “Es cuestión de tiempo que Sánchez tenga que responder ante los tribunales", ha afirmado el miembro del PP. Ante estas declaraciones, fuentes gubernamentales y de la Moncloa han negado categóricamente que Corvillo realizara funciones de chófer para Sánchez. Cabe recordar que queda menos de un mes para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre y muy pocos días para que arranque la campaña electoral.

articles.title: Mexican judge arrested after U.S. charges him of accepting $2M bribe in case linked to former Olympian
articles.summary: Luis Benítez Alcántara allegedly took a $2 million bribe to release Ryan Wedding's second-in-command in a billion-dollar cocaine enterprise.
articles.body: Luis Benítez Alcántara, a Mexican judge accused of accepting a bribe to release a transnational cocaine smuggler, was arrested in Colombia on Sunday after the U.S. charged him with nine counts of being an accessory after the fact. Benítez, according to a Thursday announcement from the U.S. Department of Justice, accepted a $2 million bribe from Canadian national Ryan Clark, who the DOJ alleges was second-in-command to former Olympic snowboarder Ryan J. Wedding in the latter's international drug dealing empire. "Benítez Alcántara was a district judge in Mexico City who allegedly accepted $2 million in exchange for granting bond to and ordering the release of Wedding’s second in command, while Wedding was orchestrating a billion-dollar transnational criminal organization and the largest supplier of cocaine to Canada with connections in Colombia, Mexico, and the U.S.," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement. US CHARGES MEXICAN GOVERNOR, TOP OFFICIALS IN CARTEL CONSPIRACY AS MEXICO FIRES BACK OVER PROOF Clark was initially arrested in Guadalajara, Mexico on Oct. 8, 2024, according to a superseding indictment. He appeared in front of Benítez for extradition proceedings on Oct. 9 after the U.S. requested his extradition. Beginning in Nov. 2024, Clark sent approximately $2.75 million to intermediaries over the course of four months, according to the indictment. On Feb. 24, 2025, Benítez received $2 million in payments from those intermediaries and granted Clark bond and release that same day, per the indictment. Among the nine counts, Benítez is charged with being an accessory after the fact to aid and abet Clark. Clark and Wedding are also charged with murder, conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute a mixture and substance containing a detectable amount of cocaine and continuing a criminal enterprise, according to the indictment. If convicted, Benítez faces up to 15 years in federal prison. "Crooked public officials, no matter where they are, who assist drug traffickers operating here at home will face justice in the United States," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement. "Thanks to the work of the Homeland Security Task Force and our international law enforcement partners, Mr. Benítez will be held accountable. The Department of Justice will continue identifying and dismantling transnational criminal organizations that threaten the safety of the American people," Blanche concluded. HIGHEST-RANKING TREN DE ARAGUA MEMBER EVER EXTRADITED TO US SET TO APPEAR IN HOUSTON COURTROOM: DOJ Despite Benítez's role in granting Clark bond and release, Mexican law enforcement officers arrested Clark again days later and handed him over to U.S. authorities on Feb. 27, 2025. Following Clark's arrest, he cooperated with FBI and U.S. officials in supplying information about his and Wedding's roles in their criminal enterprise, according to a DOJ indictment against Wedding. KASH PATEL DEFENDS FBI'S ‘MOST WANTED’ BUSTS AMID MANIPULATION ACCUSATIONS, HIGHLIGHTS 'SUMMER HEAT' SUCCESS Wedding, a former member of the FBI's Top 10 Most Wanted List, was arrested in Mexico in January 2026. In addition to running a cocaine distribution empire that the indictment alleges imported the majority of illicit cocaine into Canada, Wedding is also accused of orchestrating the murders of numerous informants and other affiliates of his illicit activities. 5 MEXICAN CARTEL BOSSES CHARGED IN WEAPONS, DRUG TRAFFICKING, TIMESHARE FRAUD SCHEMES, DOJ SAYS In January, he pleaded not guilty to federal charges of running a criminal enterprise, murder, conspiring to distribute cocaine and other crimes. His empire allegedly worked in concert with the powerful Mexican Sinaloa Cartel to move and distribute cocaine through Colombia, Mexico and the rest of North America, according to the indictment. And that ends today," FBI Director Kash Patel said in January after Wedding's arrest.

articles.title: Cruz on midterms: ‘It was an a‑‑ kicking’
articles.summary: Texas Sen. Ted Cruz (R) reflected on the results of the midterm elections in his home state and nationwide, calling the Democrats’ win a “blue tsunami.” “202...
articles.body:
Texas Sen. Ted Cruz (R) reflected on the results of the midterm elections in his home state and nationwide, calling the Democrats' win a " blue tsunami ."

"2026 was not simply a blue wave. It was a blue tsunami. It was an a‑‑ kicking," Cruz said in an episode of his podcast , "Verdict with Ted Cruz."

The Democrats won a stunning victory in the midterm elections, securing control over the House and Senate. The party notched big wins in battleground states like Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio and Michigan, flipping GOP-held seats.

In Texas, where Republicans have historically maintained a stronghold for years, Democratic candidates emerged victorious in key races. State Rep. Gina Hinojosa (D) defeated incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott to be elected as the state's first Latina governor. Abbott has served three terms, and the state has not seen a Democratic governor since Ann Richards in 1994.

The Lone Star State was also home to one of the most competitive Senate races in the country, where Democrat James Talarico defeated Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton (R) to become the first Democratic senator from the state in decades.

"Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas," Cruz said in his podcast. "In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election."

"For weeks I had been publicly warning … that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible," he added.

In the podcast, Cruz discussed issues that led to the Republicans' losses in the elections, highlighting the cost of living as a "top issue."

"Food is too high. Gas is too high. Diesel is too high. Insurance is too high. Life is too high," Cruz said. "Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long."

He pressed the need to "listen and respond" and "champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives."

In an earlier statement shared to social media, the Republican senator said that "Texans will be hurt" by the midterm results, which swayed the state in the direction of the Democrats.

"Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business," he wrote. "Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI."

articles.title: Democrat drops out of race due to health concerns and still wins; opponent says, 'We deserve to know more'
articles.summary: Democratic Iowa state House candidate Eric Armstrong, who announced in September that he was dropping his campaign due to health struggles, still won the election contest.
articles.body: A Democratic candidate who dropped his campaign for health reasons still defeated the Republican candidate in an Iowa state House race. Democrat Eric Armstrong explained in a Sept. 7 Facebook post that he was abandoning his campaign due to health issues. "Running a successful campaign requires immense physical and mental energy. Recently, I have been facing some personal health issues that require my full attention and immediate care," Armstrong wrote, in part. "Because I must prioritize my health and recovery at this time, I am stepping down from my campaign, effective immediately. This was a deeply difficult choice. However, I know it is the right one. 3 INJURED IN SHOOTING AT DES MOINES, IOWA, POST OFFICE; SUSPECT DETAINED: POLICE "Our District deserves a representative who can give 100 percent of their energy to this race. Right now, I must focus on healing so that I can continue to serve our community in other ways in the future." Despite this announcement, Armstrong's name remained on the ballot, and voters still elected him. Unofficial results indicate that Armstrong received 4,602 votes, while Republican Keith Jones, who is a member of the Pottawattamie County Board of Supervisors, received 3,737 votes. DEMOCRATS SEIZE MAJORITY OF GOVERNORS' OFFICES IN ELECTION-NIGHT SHIFT "I'm going to do my best to represent" the district, Armstrong said during a phone interview Wednesday with The New York Times. "But I still have health issues. That’s what I'm struggling with." Armstrong did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment Thursday. In part of a statement to Fox News Digital Thursday, Jones wrote, "I think we deserve to know more." "Serious rumors were that he was hiding a background that could have disqualified him from office. People ‘could have’ donated to his campaign and subsequently voted for him based on a falsehood. I was a police officer for 29 years. There's absolutely something there that needs to be investigated by the media," Jones later wrote in part of another statement provided to Fox News Digital on Thursday. "If he's truly sick, why did he reenter the race? Is he healthy enough to hold office? Did he lie about being sick to cover a damaging personal story? Public trust at that level is important. Is he qualified to be in public office?" Jones asked.
